title: Hobbies and Free Time
summary: Interests, hobbies, frequency, and arranging to meet.
whyItMatters: Hobbies are a natural way to introduce yourself, find shared interests, and make plans. A small set of activity verbs and time expressions lets you say what you enjoy, what you can do, and when you are free.

mentalModel.title: Build an activity menu
mentalModel.content: Group hobbies by what you do: sport, music, media, social activities, and quiet activities. This makes vocabulary easier to retrieve in conversation.

mentalModel.title: Attach a time to every hobby
mentalModel.content: Turn a hobby word into a useful sentence by adding when or how often: 'Ich schwimme am Samstag' or 'Ich lese oft.'

mentalModel.title: Move from interest to invitation
mentalModel.content: A short conversation can progress from 'Was machst du gern?' to a shared activity and then a meeting time.

coverageChecklist: days and parts of the day

ruleBlocks.title: Learn hobbies as activity chunks
ruleBlocks.content: Learn the complete expression you need: Fußball spielen, Musik hören, Bücher lesen, Freunde treffen, and ins Kino gehen.

ruleBlocks.title: Use gern to express enjoyment
ruleBlocks.content: Place 'gern' after the conjugated verb to say that you like doing an activity: 'Ich tanze gern.'

ruleBlocks.title: Add a simple time expression
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'am' with days and many parts of the day: am Montag, am Wochenende, am Abend. Use 'heute' and 'morgen' without 'am'.

ruleBlocks.title: Show how often
ruleBlocks.content: Use beginner frequency words such as immer, oft, manchmal, selten, and nie to describe routines.

sentenceStructure: Conjugate the activity verb in position two: 'Ich spiele Fußball.'
Place 'gern' after the conjugated verb: 'Ich spiele gern Fußball.'
A time expression can begin the sentence; the verb still remains in position two: 'Am Samstag spiele ich Fußball.'
Frequency words usually appear after the conjugated verb in simple beginner sentences: 'Ich schwimme oft.'

concepts: tell short stories about free-time experiences
explain reasons for interests and preferences

comparisons.summary: The hobby lesson names activities; the grammar lesson adds ability and possibility with 'können'.
The communication lesson turns hobbies, days, and frequency words into invitations and agreed plans.

examples.de: Am Wochenende treffe ich oft Freunde.
examples.en: I often meet friends at the weekend.

examples.de: Meine Schwester hört jeden Abend Musik.
examples.en: My sister listens to music every evening.
We rarely go to the cinema.

examples.de: Was machst du am Samstag gern?
examples.en: What do you like doing on Saturday?

commonMistakes.reason: The conjugated verb occupies position two; 'gern' follows it.
Use 'am' with days of the week.
When time is first, the conjugated verb remains in position two and the subject follows.

specialCases: 'Gern' describes enjoyment of an action; 'mögen' is often used with nouns and is developed further later.
'Lieber' expresses a preference between activities: 'Ich lese lieber.'
Some hobby expressions are separable or use fixed prepositions; learn them initially as complete chunks.
tips: Create a personal list of five real hobbies instead of memorizing an abstract list.
Practice each hobby with 'gern', one day, and one frequency word.
Ask and answer 'Was machst du gern?' with different partners or imagined profiles.

memoryHooks.title: Put hobbies on a calendar
memoryHooks.content: Imagine one activity on each day and describe the week aloud.

memoryHooks.title: Verb, gern, time
memoryHooks.content: Build sentences in three layers: the activity, enjoyment, and when it happens.
